killedBy: createGameSessionHost: start SHOWS the session it built, and shows the replacement rather than the one it retired
why: The host builds a session and never shows it -- construction and routing are deliberately separate acts here, so dropping the second leaves a world built behind a menu. Already caught by composition (four `loop.test.ts` cases red), which is why this entry is scoped to BOTH files: what was missing was the claim at the layer that owns it. `session-host.test.ts` recorded `enteredIds` -- documented as "which session was SHOWN, in order" -- and asserted it zero times, so the failure surfaced as a stale campaign run or a silent Main Menu rather than as "the host never showed what it built". The killer also pins the ORDER, which distinguishes showing the replacement from re-showing the session just retired.
